## Observed and projected population growth
We compare observed population growth with two model-based estimates: the year-specific asymptotic growth rate and the one-step projected growth rate.

For the one-step projection, we initialize each population using its observed size distribution in year (t), assigning recruits without recorded size according to the estimated recruit size distribution. We then project the population to year (t+1) using the corresponding year-specific kernel.

To keep observed and projected abundance comparable, we count individuals with valid size measurements and recruits without recorded size. Comparisons are restricted to consecutive years with available model parameters.

The results are aggregated across populations for each year, allowing us to compare observed growth with both asymptotic and one-step projected growth rates.
```{r}
# Population-year abundance ---------------------------------------------------
df_counts_population_year <- df %>%
  group_by(
    population,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(
      is.finite(logsize_t0),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      !is.finite(logsize_t0) &
        recruit == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ipm_state = n_sized +
      n_unsized_recruits,
    .groups = 'drop')


# Matched consecutive population transitions ----------------------------------
df_obs_pgr_population <- df_counts_population_year %>%
  arrange(
    population,
    year) %>%
  group_by(
    population) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n_ipm_state),
    year_gap = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_gap == 1,
    n_ipm_state > 0,
    year %in% ipm_years) %>%
  rename(
    n_t0 = n_ipm_state) %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0)


# Initial population size distribution ----------------------------------------
make_initial_n_population <- function(
    year0,
    population_i,
    pars) {

  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n

  breaks <- seq(
    L,
    U,
    length.out = n + 1)

  b <- L + c(0:n) * h

  y <- 0.5 *
    (b[1:n] +
       b[2:(n + 1)])

  df0 <- df %>%
    filter(
      year == year0,
      population == population_i)

  sizes <- df0 %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
    pull(
      logsize_t0)

  size_counts <- hist(
    pmin(
      pmax(
        sizes,
        L),
      U),
    breaks = breaks,
    plot = FALSE,
    include.lowest = TRUE)$counts

  n_density <- size_counts /
    h

  n_unsized_recruits <- df0 %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(
        !is.finite(logsize_t0) &
          recruit == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(n)

  if (n_unsized_recruits > 0) {
    recr_y <- dnorm(
      y,
      mean = pars$recr_sz,
      sd = pars$recr_sd)

    recr_y <- recr_y /
      sum(recr_y * h)

    n_density <- n_density +
      n_unsized_recruits *
      recr_y
  }

  n_density
}


# Project one population-year -------------------------------------------------
project_one_population_year <- function(
    yr,
    population_i) {

  pars_y <- make_ipm_pars(
    year = yr,
    re_year_t1 = yr + 1L)

  n_obs <- make_initial_n_population(
    year0 = yr,
    population_i = population_i,
    pars = pars_y)

  K <- kernel(
    pars_y)$k_yx

  h <- (pars_y$U - pars_y$L) /
    pars_y$mat_siz

  n_initial <- sum(n_obs) *
    h

  n_proj <- K %*%
    n_obs

  n_projected <- sum(n_proj) *
    h

  data.frame(
    year = yr,
    population = population_i,
    n_obs_model = n_initial,
    n_proj_model = n_projected,
    asym_lambda = Re(
      eigen(K)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = as.numeric(
      n_projected /
        n_initial))
}


# Project all matched population transitions ----------------------------------
df_proj_population <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(df_obs_pgr_population)),
    function(i) {

      project_one_population_year(
        yr = df_obs_pgr_population$year[i],
        population_i =
          df_obs_pgr_population$population[i])
    }))


# Population-level observed and modeled growth --------------------------------
df_compare_population <- df_obs_pgr_population %>%
  left_join(
    df_proj_population,
    by = c(
      'year',
      'population')) %>%
  mutate(
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs =
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs =
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr)


# Whole-population annual comparison ------------------------------------------
df_compare <- df_compare_population %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(
      asym_lambda,
      w = n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = sum(
      n_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t1 = sum(
      n_t1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs_model = sum(
      n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proj_model = sum(
      n_proj_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_populations = n(),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 /
      n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model /
      n_obs_model)
```

# Yearly IPM {#ipm_yr}

## Introduction
We compare observed population growth with two model-based estimates: the year-specific asymptotic growth rate and the one-step projected growth rate.

For the one-step projection, we initialize each population using its observed size distribution in year (t), assigning recruits without recorded size according to the estimated recruit size distribution. We then project the population to year (t+1) using the corresponding year-specific kernel.

To keep observed and projected abundance comparable, we count individuals with valid size measurements and recruits without recorded size. Comparisons are restricted to consecutive years with available model parameters.

The results are aggregated across populations for each year, allowing us to compare observed growth with both asymptotic and one-step projected growth rates.

## Specifications
For survival, growth, dormancy entry, flowering, and seed production probability, we consider intercept-only, linear, quadratic, and cubic relationships with log leaf area. Model selection is based on AICc, with the option to manually specify a model.

We include year as a random intercept in most vital-rate models. For growth, both the intercept and linear size effect vary among years. Seed number is modelled using intercept-only, linear, and quadratic alternatives.
```{r}
v_mod_set_su   <- c()
v_mod_set_gr   <- c()
v_mod_set_do   <- c()
v_mod_set_fl   <- c()
v_mod_set_se   <- c()
v_mod_set_se_n <- c()

# Controls
ctrl_glmer <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

ctrl_lmer <- lmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa', optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

```

## Data
```{r}
df <- read.csv(
  file.path(
    dir_data,
    paste0(v_head, '_', v_sp_abb, '_df_workdata.csv'))) %>%
  mutate(year = as.integer(year), year_t1 = as.integer(year_t1)) %>%
  filter(state %in% v_states, !is.na(year), !(year %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  # Remove the inspected duplicate empty 2001 -> 2001 row only.
  filter(!(population == 30 & id == 354 & year == 2001 &
             year_t1 %in% 2001L))
```

## Vital rates
### Survival
#### Data
```{r}
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography, dormant_t0 == 0, !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 > 0, is.finite(logsize_t0),
    is.finite(logsize_t0_2), is.finite(logsize_t0_3),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    state, population, id, year, size_t0, survives,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3)
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_su_0 <- glmer(
  survives ~ 1 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_su_1 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_su_2 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_su_3 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_1, mod_su_2, mod_su_3)
mods_su_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc
mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su}

mod_su_best <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]
mod_su_ranef <- coef(mod_su_best)$year

mod_su_best
summary(mod_su_best)
mods_su_dAICc
```

#### Plots by year
```{r}
make_su_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_su %>% filter(year == year_i)
  x <- seq(
    min(df_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df_i$logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)

  pred_i <- tibble(logsize_t0 = x) %>%
    mutate(
      logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
      logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3,
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_su$year)))

  pred_i$survives <- predict(
    mod_su_best, newdata = pred_i, type = 'response', re.form = NULL)

  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logsize_t0, breaks = 8, include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
    group_by(bin) %>%
    summarise(
      logsize_t0 = mean(logsize_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      survives = mean(survives, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
    filter(!is.na(logsize_t0), n > 0)

  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i, aes(logsize_t0, survives), size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i, aes(logsize_t0, survives), linewidth = 0.7) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression('log(leaf area)'[t0]),
      y = 'Survival probability') +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = 'none')}

su_yrs <- lapply(levels(df_su$year), make_su_year_plot)
fig_su_years <- wrap_plots(su_yrs) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = 'Survival - year specific',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = 'bold'),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)))

fig_su_years
```

### Dormant survival and reactivation
Dormant survival and reactivation are estimated separately, using year-specific random intercepts when the response contains variation. If the response is constant, we instead use an intercept-only binomial model.

Both processes remain independent of plant size.
```{r}
df_dorm_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography, dormant_t0 == 1, !is.na(survives),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year))

# A constant response cannot estimate a year random effect.
if (n_distinct(df_dorm_su$survives) > 1) {
  mod_dorm_su <- glmer(
    survives ~ 1 + (1 | year),
    data = df_dorm_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
} else {
  mod_dorm_su <- glm(
    survives ~ 1, data = df_dorm_su, family = binomial)}

mod_dorm_su
summary(mod_dorm_su)


df_ra <- df_dorm_su %>%
  filter(survives == 1, !is.na(dormant_t1)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(as.character(year)),
    reactivate = as.integer(dormant_t1 == 0))

if (n_distinct(df_ra$reactivate) > 1) {
  mod_ra <- glmer(
    reactivate ~ 1 + (1 | year),
    data = df_ra, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
} else {
  mod_ra <- glm(
    reactivate ~ 1, data = df_ra, family = binomial)}

mod_ra
summary(mod_ra)


df_ra_size <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography, dormant_t0 == 1, survives == 1,
    dormant_t1 == 0, size_t1 > 0, is.finite(logsize_t1),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(logsize_reactivate = logsize_t1)

react_sz <- mean(df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate, na.rm = TRUE)
react_sd <- sd(df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate, na.rm = TRUE)
```

### Seed production probability
#### Data
```{r}
# Probability of positive seed production, conditional on flowering.
df_se <- df %>%
  filter(
    flower == 1, !is.na(seed_nr), size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0), is.finite(logsize_t0_2),
    is.finite(logsize_t0_3)) %>%
  mutate(year = factor(year), seed_prod = as.integer(seed_nr > 0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    state, population, id, year, size_t0, flower, seed_prod, seed_nr,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3)
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_se_0 <- glmer(
  seed_prod ~ 1 + (1 | year),
  data = df_se, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_se_1 <- glmer(
  seed_prod ~ logsize_t0 + (1 | year),
  data = df_se, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_se_2 <- glmer(
  seed_prod ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + (1 | year),
  data = df_se, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_se_3 <- glmer(
  seed_prod ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3 + (1 | year),
  data = df_se, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)

mods_se <- list(
  mod_se_0, mod_se_1, mod_se_2, mod_se_3)
mods_se_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_se, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc
mods_se_sorted <- order(mods_se_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_se) == 0) {
  mod_se_index_bestfit <- mods_se_sorted[1]
  v_mod_se_index <- mod_se_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_se_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_se + 1
  v_mod_se_index <- v_mod_set_se}

mod_se_best <- mods_se[[mod_se_index_bestfit]]
mod_se_ranef <- coef(mod_se_best)$year

mod_se_best
summary(mod_se_best)
mods_se_dAICc
```

Seed number is estimated using negative-binomial mixed models with a random intercept for year. We consider up to quadratic size effects, while the cubic model is excluded from the current model selection.

### Seed to recruit transition
Recruitment is estimated at the population-year level, relating total seed production in year (t) to newly observed seedlings in year (t+2). We use a negative-binomial mixed model with total seed production as an offset and a random intercept for the year in which recruits appear.

The resulting year-specific recruitment rate represents the expected number of recruits per observed seed. This rate is applied to the seed cohort already present in the IPM, while newly produced seeds contribute recruits only after the two-year delay.
```{r}
# Seeds produced in year t are related to recruits observed in year t + 2.
df_re_seed <- df %>%
  group_by(population, year) %>%
  summarise(
    nr_seeds = if (all(is.na(seed_nr))) NA_real_ else
      sum(seed_nr, na.rm = TRUE),
    nr_seed_obs = sum(!is.na(seed_nr)), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(year_t2 = year + 2L)


df_re_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(population, year)

df_re_count <- df %>%
  filter(recruit == 1) %>%
  count(population, year, name = 'nr_recruits')

df_re_count <- df_re_sampled %>%
  left_join(df_re_count, by = c('population', 'year')) %>%
  mutate(nr_recruits = replace_na(nr_recruits, 0L))


df_re <- df_re_seed %>%
  inner_join(df_re_count, by = c('population', 'year_t2' = 'year')) %>%
  filter(nr_seed_obs > 0) %>%
  mutate(recruit_year = factor(year_t2))
```

#### Seed to recruit model
```{r}
# The offset gives recruits per seed; the year effect is for recruit arrival.
df_re_mod <- df_re %>%
  filter(nr_seeds > 0) %>%
  mutate(recruit_year = factor(as.character(recruit_year)))

mod_re_best <- glmer.nb(
  nr_recruits ~ 1 + offset(log(nr_seeds)) + (1 | recruit_year),
  data = df_re_mod, control = ctrl_glmer)

mod_re_ranef <- coef(mod_re_best)$recruit_year
recr_per_seed <- exp(unname(fixef(mod_re_best)['(Intercept)']))

mod_re_best
summary(mod_re_best)
recr_per_seed
```

## Parameter extraction helpers
```{r}
empty_coef_df <- function() {
  data.frame(coefficient = character(), value = numeric())}

is_mixed_model <- function(model) {
  inherits(model, 'merMod')}

get_fixef_safe <- function(model) {
  if (is_mixed_model(model)) fixef(model) else coef(model)}

get_group_coef_safe <- function(model, group_var) {
  if (!is_mixed_model(model)) return(NULL)
  coef(model)[[group_var]]}

find_model_term <- function(model_terms, aliases) {
  for (alias in unlist(aliases)) {
    if (grepl('^regex:', alias)) {
      hit <- grep(sub('^regex:', '', alias), model_terms, value = TRUE)
    } else {
      hit <- model_terms[model_terms == alias]}
    if (length(hit) > 0) return(hit[1])}
  NA_character_}

bind_coef_rows <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!vapply(x, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(x) == 0) return(empty_coef_df())
  out <- do.call(rbind, x)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out}

coef_df_to_list <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) return(list())
  x %>%
    mutate(coefficient = as.character(coefficient)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = coefficient, values_from = value) %>%
    as.list()}

extract_fixed_pars <- function(model, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  model_coefs <- get_fixef_safe(model)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_name) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(names(model_coefs), term_map[[coef_name]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (!fill_missing) return(NULL)
      value <- 0
    } else {
      value <- unname(model_coefs[model_term])}
    data.frame(coefficient = coef_name, value = value)})
  bind_coef_rows(out)}

extract_group_pars <- function(
    model, group_var, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  coef_matrix <- get_group_coef_safe(model, group_var)
  if (is.null(coef_matrix)) return(empty_coef_df())
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_prefix) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(
      colnames(coef_matrix), term_map[[coef_prefix]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (!fill_missing) return(NULL)
      value <- rep(0, nrow(coef_matrix))
    } else {
      value <- coef_matrix[, model_term]}
    data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0(coef_prefix, '_', rownames(coef_matrix)),
      value = value)})
  bind_coef_rows(out)}

extract_re_ranef_devs <- function(model, group_var, group_label) {
  ranef_matrix <- ranef(model)[[group_var]]
  data.frame(
    coefficient = paste0('re_u0_', group_label, '_', rownames(ranef_matrix)),
    value = ranef_matrix[, '(Intercept)'])}


# Term maps -------------------------------------------------------------------
size_term_map <- list(
  b0 = c('(Intercept)'),
  b1 = c('logsize_t0'),
  b2 = c('logsize_t0_2', 'I(logsize_t0^2)'),
  b3 = c('logsize_t0_3', 'I(logsize_t0^3)'))

make_term_map <- function(prefix, map) {
  out <- map
  names(out) <- paste0(prefix, names(out))
  out}

su_term_map <- make_term_map('surv_', size_term_map)

re_term_map <- list(re_b0 = c('(Intercept)'))

do_fe <- extract_fixed_pars(mod_do_best, do_term_map)
fl_fe <- extract_fixed_pars(mod_fl_best, fl_term_map)

re_fe <- extract_fixed_pars(mod_re_best, re_term_map)

p_dorm_survival <- plogis(
  unname(get_fixef_safe(mod_dorm_su)['(Intercept)']))
p_reactivate <- plogis(
  unname(get_fixef_safe(mod_ra)['(Intercept)']))


# Constants -------------------------------------------------------------------
gr_var_coef <- coef(mod_gr_var)
mesh_limits <- range(
  c(df$logsize_t0, df_gr$logsize_t1, df_ra_size$logsize_reactivate),
  na.rm = TRUE, finite = TRUE)

constants <- tibble::tribble(
  ~coefficient, ~value,
  'recr_sz', recr_sz,

pars_cons <- bind_coef_rows(list(

pars_all_mean <- coef_df_to_list(pars_cons)
pars_mean <- pars_all_mean
```

## IPM helper functions
```{r}
inv_logit <- function(x) {
  plogis(x)}

get_par <- function(pars, par_name, default = 0) {
  if (!is.null(pars[[par_name]])) return(pars[[par_name]])
  default}

make_ipm_pars <- function(
    pars_mean, pars_year = NULL, pars_re_year = NULL,
    year = NULL, recruit_year = NULL) {
  pars <- pars_mean

  if (!is.null(year) && !is.null(pars_year)) {
    year <- as.character(year)
    year_hits <- grep(paste0('_', year, '$'), names(pars_year), value = TRUE)
    for (nm in year_hits) {
      base_nm <- sub(paste0('_', year, '$'), '', nm)
      pars[[base_nm]] <- pars_year[[nm]]}}

  # K_t recruits the seed cohort from t-1 into plants at t+1.
  if (is.null(recruit_year) && !is.null(year)) {
    recruit_year <- as.integer(year) + 1L}

  if (!is.null(recruit_year) && !is.null(pars_re_year)) {
    pars$re_b0 <- get_par(pars, 're_b0') + get_par(
      pars_re_year, paste0('re_u0_recruit_year_', recruit_year))}

  pars}

surv_lp <- function(x, pars) {
  get_par(pars, 'surv_b0') + get_par(pars, 'surv_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'surv_b3') * x^3}

sx <- function(x, pars) {
  inv_logit(surv_lp(x, pars))}

grow_mu <- function(x, pars) {
  get_par(pars, 'grow_b0') + get_par(pars, 'grow_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'grow_b3') * x^3}

# Variance was fitted against fitted next-year size, not starting size.
grow_sd <- function(x, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * grow_mu(x, pars)))}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars) {
  dnorm(y, mean = grow_mu(x, pars), sd = grow_sd(x, pars))}

dx <- function(x, pars) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'dorm_b0') + get_par(pars, 'dorm_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'dorm_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'dorm_b3') * x^3
  inv_logit(eta)}

fl_x <- function(x, pars) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'fl_b0') + get_par(pars, 'fl_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'fl_b3') * x^3
  inv_logit(eta)}

se_x <- function(x, pars) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'se_b0') + get_par(pars, 'se_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'se_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'se_b3') * x^3
  inv_logit(eta)}

se_n_x <- function(x, pars) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'se_n_b0') + get_par(pars, 'se_n_b1') * x +
    get_par(pars, 'se_n_b2') * x^2 + get_par(pars, 'se_n_b3') * x^3
  exp(eta)}

seedx <- function(x, pars) {
  fl_x(x, pars) * se_x(x, pars) * se_n_x(x, pars)}

re_per_seed <- function(pars) {
  exp(get_par(pars, 're_b0'))}

re_y_dist <- function(y, pars, h = NULL) {
  dens <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd)
  if (!is.null(h)) dens <- dens / sum(dens * h)
  dens}

ra_y_dist <- function(y, pars, h = NULL) {
  dens <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$react_sz, sd = pars$react_sd)
  if (!is.null(h)) dens <- dens / sum(dens * h)
  dens}

pxy <- function(x, y, pars) {
  sx(x, pars) * (1 - dx(x, pars)) * gxy(x, y, pars)}
```

## Kernel
We retain the continuous size structure with 200 mesh points and two additional discrete states for dormant plants and the delayed seed cohort.

The kernel combines survival, growth, dormancy entry, dormant survival, reactivation, and recruitment. Seeds produced by active plants enter the seed state in the following year and contribute recruits one year later. The seed-to-recruit rate accounts for losses between observed seed production and seedling establishment.
```{r}
# State order: active size-bin counts, dormant count, delayed seed cohort.
# Rows = t+1; columns = t. Plants t -> seed cohort t+1 -> recruits t+2.
# The seed state carries production equivalents; re_per_seed includes losses.
kernel <- function(pars) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])

  i_dorm <- n + 1
  i_seed <- n + 2
  Smat <- sx(y, pars)
  Dvec <- dx(y, pars)
  Gmat <- t(outer(y, y, gxy, pars)) * h

  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    if (i <= n / 2) {
      Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    } else {
      Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])}}

  Tmat <- sweep(Gmat, 2, Smat * (1 - Dvec), '*')
  react_y <- ra_y_dist(y, pars, h = h) * h
  recr_y <- re_y_dist(y, pars, h = h) * h

  Pmat <- matrix(0, n + 2, n + 2)
  Fmat <- matrix(0, n + 2, n + 2)

  Pmat[1:n, 1:n] <- Tmat
  Pmat[i_dorm, 1:n] <- Smat * Dvec
  Pmat[1:n, i_dorm] <-
    pars$p_dorm_survival * pars$p_reactivate * react_y
  Pmat[i_dorm, i_dorm] <-
    pars$p_dorm_survival * (1 - pars$p_reactivate)

  Fmat[i_seed, 1:n] <- seedx(y, pars)
  Pmat[1:n, i_seed] <- re_per_seed(pars) * recr_y

  k_yx <- Pmat + Fmat

  list(
    k_yx = k_yx, Pmat = Pmat, Fmat = Fmat, Tmat = Tmat,
    Gmat = Gmat, Smat = Smat, Dvec = Dvec, meshpts = y,
    dormant_index = i_dorm, seed_index = i_seed, h = h, L = L, U = U)}

lambda_ipm <- function(pars) {
  Re(eigen(kernel(pars)$k_yx)$values[1])}
```

## Mean IPM
```{r}
lam_mean <- lambda_ipm(pars_mean)
lam_mean
```

## Year-specific IPMs
```{r}
lambda_ipm_year <- function(year, recruit_year = NULL) {
  pars_i <- make_ipm_pars(
    pars_mean = pars_all_mean, pars_year = pars_all_year,
    pars_re_year = pars_all_re_year, year = year,
    recruit_year = recruit_year)
  lambda_ipm(pars_i)}

# Retain years represented in all fitted yearly processes.
ipm_years <- sort(Reduce(intersect, list(
  as.integer(levels(df_su$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_gr$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_do$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_dorm_su$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_ra$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_fl$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_se$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_se_n$year)),
  as.integer(levels(df_re_mod$recruit_year)) - 1L)))

lambda_year <- data.frame(
  year = ipm_years,
  lambda = sapply(ipm_years, lambda_ipm_year))

fig_lambda_year <- ggplot(lambda_year, aes(year, lambda)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = 'dashed') +
  geom_point() +
  geom_line() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = 'Year-specific asymptotic lambda', subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = 'Year', y = expression(lambda))

fig_lambda_year
```

## Observed and projected population growth
```{r}
# Match populations at both censuses within the reliable demographic period.
# Plant counts include active plants and dormant plants, but not seeds.
last_reliable_t1 <- max(
  df$year_t1[df$reliable_demography %in% TRUE], na.rm = TRUE)


# Population-year abundance ---------------------------------------------------
# As in POLE, include sized active plants and unsized recruits; add dormancy.
df_counts_population_year <- df %>%
  filter(year <= last_reliable_t1) %>%
  group_by(population, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(dormant_t0 == 0 & is.finite(logsize_t0), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      dormant_t0 == 0 & !is.finite(logsize_t0) & recruit == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_dormant = sum(dormant_t0 == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ipm_state = n_sized + n_unsized_recruits + n_dormant,
    .groups = 'drop')


# Matched consecutive population transitions ----------------------------------
df_obs_pgr_population <- df_counts_population_year %>%
  arrange(population, year) %>%
  group_by(population) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year), n_t1 = lead(n_ipm_state),
    year_gap = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(year_gap == 1, n_ipm_state > 0, year %in% ipm_years) %>%
  rename(n_t0 = n_ipm_state) %>%
  inner_join(
    df_re_seed %>%
      filter(nr_seed_obs > 0) %>%
      transmute(population, year = year + 1L, seeds_prev = nr_seeds),
    by = c('population', 'year')) %>%
  mutate(obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0)


# Initial population size distribution ----------------------------------------
make_initial_n_population <- function(year0, population_i, pars) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  breaks <- seq(L, U, length.out = n + 1)
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])

  df0 <- df %>% filter(year == year0, population == population_i)
  sizes <- df0 %>%
    filter(dormant_t0 == 0, is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
    pull(logsize_t0)

  size_counts <- hist(
    pmin(pmax(sizes, L), U), breaks = breaks,
    plot = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)$counts

  n_unsized_recruits <- sum(
    df0$dormant_t0 == 0 & !is.finite(df0$logsize_t0) & df0$recruit == 1,
    na.rm = TRUE)
  size_counts <- size_counts +
    n_unsized_recruits * re_y_dist(y, pars, h = h) * h

  n_dormant <- sum(df0$dormant_t0 == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_seed <- df_re_seed %>%
    filter(population == population_i, year == year0 - 1L) %>%
    pull(nr_seeds)

  c(size_counts, n_dormant, n_seed)}


# Project one population-year -------------------------------------------------
# The initial seed cohort uses observed production in t-1.
# Seeds predicted during t affect plant abundance at t+2, not t+1.
project_one_population_year <- function(yr, population_i) {
  pars_y <- make_ipm_pars(
    pars_mean = pars_all_mean, pars_year = pars_all_year,
    pars_re_year = pars_all_re_year, year = yr, recruit_year = yr + 1L)

  n_obs <- make_initial_n_population(
    year0 = yr, population_i = population_i, pars = pars_y)
  K <- kernel(pars_y)$k_yx
  n_proj <- K %*% n_obs

  plant_indices <- seq_len(pars_y$mat_siz + 1)
  n_initial <- sum(n_obs[plant_indices])
  n_projected <- sum(n_proj[plant_indices])

  data.frame(
    year = yr, population = population_i,
    n_obs_model = n_initial, n_proj_model = n_projected,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = as.numeric(n_projected / n_initial))}


# Project all matched population transitions ----------------------------------
df_proj_population <- bind_rows(lapply(
  seq_len(nrow(df_obs_pgr_population)), function(i) {
    project_one_population_year(
      yr = df_obs_pgr_population$year[i],
      population_i = df_obs_pgr_population$population[i])}))


# Population-level observed and modeled growth ---------------------------------
df_compare_population <- df_obs_pgr_population %>%
  left_join(df_proj_population, by = c('year', 'population')) %>%
  mutate(
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs = asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs = proj_lambda - obs_pgr)


# Whole-population annual comparison ------------------------------------------
df_compare <- df_compare_population %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(asym_lambda, w = n_obs_model),
    n_t0 = sum(n_t0), n_t1 = sum(n_t1),
    n_obs_model = sum(n_obs_model), n_proj_model = sum(n_proj_model),
    n_populations = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model / n_obs_model)
```

# Mean mega matrix 2x2 {#mean_mega}

## Introduction
### Conceptual framework of the mega-matrix integral projection model

#### Model structure and demographic states

To incorporate above-ground dormancy into the population dynamics of *Panax quinquefolius*, we extended a conventional size-structured integral projection model (IPM) into a **mega-matrix framework**. While a conventional IPM describes demographic transitions as functions of a continuous state variable, typically individual size, the mega-matrix combines multiple demographic states within a single projection operator. This allows the model to account for individuals that temporarily disappear from the above-ground population without necessarily dying.

The model distinguishes between two demographic states: **active individuals**, which are present above ground and can be assigned a measurable size, and **dormant individuals**, which remain alive but have no measurable above-ground size. The primary challenge in representing dormancy is that the continuous size variable used to predict demographic transitions becomes unavailable during the dormant period. Simply removing dormant individuals from the size distribution would discard information about their previous condition, while assigning them an arbitrary size would introduce an artificial size transition.

To address this, the mega-matrix uses a **size-memory approach**, in which dormant individuals retain the size they had at their last active census. The dormant state therefore represents a distribution of remembered sizes rather than actual sizes during dormancy. This information is preserved until the individual either reactivates or leaves the modeled population.

The population is consequently represented by two coupled size distributions: the active population, structured by current size, and the dormant population, structured by size before dormancy.

#### Mega-matrix formulation

The population is projected between consecutive annual censuses using the following matrix:

\[
\mathbf{n}_{t+1} =
\underbrace{
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{T}+\mathbf{F} & \mathbf{R}\\
\mathbf{E} & \mathbf{0}
\end{pmatrix}
}_{\mathbf{K}}
\mathbf{n}_t
\]

where \(\mathbf{n}_t\) contains the active and dormant size distributions at time \(t\), and \(\mathbf{K}\) is the complete projection operator.

Each block represents a distinct demographic transition. Columns correspond to the demographic state of origin, whereas rows describe the destination state at the next census.

The upper-left block, \(\mathbf{T}+\mathbf{F}\), represents the conventional active population, combining survival and growth of established individuals with the production of new recruits. The lower-left block, \(\mathbf{E}\), represents entry into dormancy. The upper-right block, \(\mathbf{R}\), describes the return of dormant individuals to the active population. Finally, the lower-right block is set to zero, excluding transitions in which individuals remain dormant over consecutive annual intervals.

This structure allows active and dormant individuals to be projected simultaneously, while retaining the continuous size information needed for subsequent demographic transitions.

##### Active survival and growth

For individuals remaining active between consecutive censuses, the transition kernel combines survival probability, the probability of avoiding dormancy, and the conditional growth distribution:

\[
T(y,x)=s(x)[1-d(x)]g(y\mid x)
\]

Here, \(x\) denotes log-transformed individual size at the current census, \(y\) denotes size at the following census, \(s(x)\) is the probability of survival, and \(d(x)\) is the probability of entering dormancy conditional on survival. The function \(g(y\mid x)\) describes the probability density of transitioning from size \(x\) to size \(y\).

Growth is represented by a continuous probability distribution that allows both increases and decreases in individual size. Its expected value depends on the individual's initial size, while the variance is also allowed to vary with size. Consequently, individuals with the same initial size can transition to different sizes at the following census.

Multiplying the growth distribution by survival and the probability of remaining active ensures that only individuals surviving without entering dormancy contribute to this part of the kernel.

##### Entry into dormancy and retention of size information

Dormancy entry is represented by a separate transition kernel:

\[
E(y,x)=s(x)d(x)\delta(y-x)
\]

where \(\delta(y-x)\) denotes a transition that preserves the individual's original size class.

In the discretized mega-matrix, this is implemented as a **diagonal matrix**. An active individual entering dormancy is transferred to the corresponding size class in the dormant distribution, without being assigned a new size.

Importantly, this transition does not imply that the individual's physical size remains unchanged underground. Instead, the dormant size class acts as a memory of the individual's condition immediately before dormancy.

This distinction is essential because it allows the model to retain information about individual size without requiring an unobservable growth process during dormancy. The dormant population therefore carries forward the distribution of sizes at dormancy entry.

##### Reactivation and the recovery of an active size distribution

When a dormant individual returns to the active population, its new size is described by a reactivation kernel:

\[
R(y,x)=s_Dr_Dg_R(y\mid x)
\]

where \(s_D\) represents survival during dormancy, \(r_D\) is the probability of reactivation conditional on survival, and \(g_R(y\mid x)\) is the conditional size distribution upon reactivation.

Unlike dormancy entry, reactivation is not restricted to the original size class. Instead, the expected size upon reactivation is determined by a regression relationship with the remembered size before dormancy:

\[
\mu_R(x)=\alpha_R+\beta_Rx
\]

The resulting reactivation-size distribution is modeled using a normal probability density centered on this expected size, with residual variation allowing individuals to return at sizes different from those predicted by their previous condition.

Thus, the reactivation kernel performs two distinct operations. First, the product of dormant survival and reactivation probability determines the proportion of dormant individuals returning to the active population. Second, the conditional size distribution determines how those returning individuals are distributed across the active size classes.

This preserves the influence of historical individual size while allowing for changes in size associated with the dormant period.

##### Duration of dormancy and the zero kernel

The lower-right block of the mega-matrix is defined as:

\[
\mathbf{K}_{DD}=\mathbf{0}
\]

This imposes a specific assumption on the duration of dormancy. Individuals can enter the dormant state during one annual transition and return to the active state during the following transition, but they cannot remain in the dormant state for another census interval.

The resulting sequence is:

\[
A_t(x)
\longrightarrow
D_{t+1}(x)
\longrightarrow
A_{t+2}(y)
\]

An individual may therefore be active at time \(t\), absent above ground at time \(t+1\), and active again at time \(t+2\).

The model consequently permits **one dormant census between two active observations**, corresponding to a two-year interval between the last observed active size and the reactivation size.

Dormant individuals that do not reactivate during the permitted transition are removed from the projected population. This includes both mortality during dormancy and individuals that survive but fail to reactivate. The latter are treated as demographic losses by assumption, rather than explicitly modeled as remaining dormant.

The zero block therefore simplifies the dormancy process by imposing a maximum duration without requiring additional states for successive years of dormancy.

#### Reproduction and recruitment

Reproduction is incorporated into the upper-left block through a fecundity kernel, \(\mathbf{F}\), which describes the contribution of active individuals to the next generation.

Expected seed production is modeled as a sequence of conditional demographic processes: the probability of flowering, the probability of producing seeds conditional on flowering, and the expected number of seeds conditional on successful seed production. These components are combined to determine expected seed production as a function of individual size.

Seed production is subsequently linked to the number of recruits observed at the following annual census. Unlike a model with an explicit seed-bank state, seeds are not retained as a separate population compartment. Instead, their contribution is transferred directly into the active size distribution at time \(t+1\).

The recruitment relationship includes both a seed-dependent component and an intercept. Because the intercept originates from a population-level recruitment relationship, it is distributed across the reference mean number of active individuals when incorporated into the individual-level fecundity kernel. This preserves the linear projection structure and reproduces the population-level intercept at the reference abundance. Its total contribution therefore scales with active population abundance rather than remaining constant across population sizes.

New recruits are assigned sizes according to a separate recruit-size distribution, independent of parental size. The fecundity kernel consequently combines expected recruitment with the probability distribution of sizes at which new individuals enter the active population.

#### Numerical implementation and population projection

The continuous size domain is discretized into equally spaced size classes for numerical implementation. Both the active and dormant components use the same size boundaries, ensuring that dormancy entry can preserve size information through a direct correspondence between classes.

The complete projection matrix consists of four blocks, each spanning the same number of size classes. The implementation uses 200 classes for each demographic state, resulting in a 400 × 400 projection matrix.

Continuous transition densities for growth, recruitment, and reactivation are converted into discrete transition probabilities. Boundary corrections are applied to account for probability mass outside the modeled size domain, preventing artificial losses caused by numerical truncation.

The complete matrix is constructed by combining the survival-transition matrix with the fecundity matrix:

\[
\mathbf{K}=\mathbf{P}+\mathbf{F}
\]

Repeated multiplication of the population vector by \(\mathbf{K}\) describes the projected development of both active and dormant size distributions through time.

Under the deterministic, density-independent formulation, the long-term population growth rate, \(\lambda\), is determined by the dominant eigenvalue of the projection matrix. This integrates the contributions of survival, growth, dormancy entry, reactivation, and recruitment into a single measure of asymptotic population growth.

Overall, the mega-matrix extends the conventional size-structured IPM by explicitly representing temporary dormancy while preserving information about individual size. Its central feature is the separation of **current size in active individuals from remembered size in dormant individuals**, allowing dormancy and subsequent reactivation to be incorporated without assigning an artificial current size to plants that are not present above ground.


## Specifications

```{r}
v_mod_set_gr   <- c()
v_mod_set_do   <- c()

v_mod_set_se_n <- c()
```

## Vital rates
### Survival
#### Data
```{r}
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 0,
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    state, population, id, year, size_t0, survives,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3)
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_su_0 <- glm(
  survives ~ 1,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_1 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_2 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_3 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_1, mod_su_2, mod_su_3)

mods_su_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su}

mod_su_bestfit <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]

mod_su_bestfit
mods_su_dAICc
```

### Growth 
#### Data
```{r}
df_gr <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    survives == 1,
    dormant_t0 == 0,
    dormant_t1 == 0,
    size_t0 > 0,
    size_t1 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0),
    is.finite(logsize_t1)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    state, population, id, year, size_t0, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3)
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_gr_0 <- lm(
  logsize_t1 ~ 1,
  data = df_gr)

mod_gr_1 <- lm(
  logsize_t1 ~ logsize_t0,
  data = df_gr)

mod_gr_2 <- lm(
  logsize_t1 ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_gr)

mod_gr_3 <- lm(
  logsize_t1 ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_gr)

mods_gr <- list(
  mod_gr_0, mod_gr_1, mod_gr_2, mod_gr_3)

mods_gr_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_gr, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_gr_sorted <- order(mods_gr_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_gr) == 0) {
  mod_gr_index_bestfit <- mods_gr_sorted[1]
  v_mod_gr_index <- mod_gr_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_gr_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_gr + 1
  v_mod_gr_index <- v_mod_set_gr}

mod_gr_bestfit <- mods_gr[[mod_gr_index_bestfit]]

mod_gr_bestfit
mods_gr_dAICc
```

### Dormant survival and reactivation
```{r}
# An active census, a gap, or an unconfirmed transition starts a new episode.
df_do_history <- df %>%
  group_by(state, population, id) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    dormancy_spell = cumsum(
      coalesce(dormant_t0 != 1, TRUE) |
        coalesce(year != lag(year_t1), TRUE) |
        !coalesce(lag(
          reliable_demography & survives == 1 & dormant_t1 == 1 &
            year_t1 == year + 1L), FALSE))) %>%
  ungroup()

# Identify entry even when the last active size was not measured.
# year_entry is the last active census; the first dormant census is +1.
df_do_entry <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography, dormant_t0 == 0, dormant_t1 == 1,
    survives == 1, year_t1 == year + 1L) %>%
  transmute(state, population, id, dormancy_spell, year_entry = year)

df_do_history <- df_do_history %>%
  left_join(
    df_do_entry, by = c("state", "population", "id", "dormancy_spell")) %>%
  mutate(dormancy_year = if_else(
    dormant_t0 == 1, as.integer(year - year_entry), NA_integer_))

df_ra <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    !is.na(survives))

# Share one annual dormant-survival estimate across both dormant stages.
mod_dorm_su <- glm(
  survives ~ 1,
  data = df_ra,
  family = "binomial")

p_dorm_survival <- predict(
  mod_dorm_su,
  newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
  type = "response")[1]


df_ra <- df_ra %>%
  filter(
    survives == 1,
    !is.na(dormant_t1)) %>%
  mutate(
    reactivate = as.integer(dormant_t1 == 0))

# Estimate first-year return from all surviving D1 transitions.
# Surviving D2 plants must return under the imposed two-census limit.
df_ra_1 <- df_ra %>%
  filter(dormancy_year == 1L)

mod_ra <- glm(
  reactivate ~ 1,
  data = df_ra_1,
  family = "binomial")

p_reactivate_1 <- predict(
  mod_ra,
  newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
  type = "response")[1]

# Diagnose observed spells extending beyond the imposed two-census limit.
# Include a confirmed D2 -> D3 even if no later source census is available.
df_dorm_over2 <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    dormancy_year > 2L |
      (dormancy_year == 2L & reliable_demography & survives == 1 &
         dormant_t1 == 1 & year_t1 == year + 1L)) %>%
  distinct(state, population, id, dormancy_spell)

df_ra %>%
  count(dormancy_year, reactivate, name = "n_transitions")

nrow(df_dorm_over2)


df_ra_size <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    survives == 1,
    dormant_t1 == 0,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    dormancy_year %in% c(1L, 2L),
    size_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_reactivate = log(size_t1))
```

### Dormancy entry vs reactivation size
```{r}
# Fit return size to completed one- or two-census dormancy episodes.
# Longer observed spells are counted above, not relabelled as two years.

df_do_entry_size <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 0,
    dormant_t1 == 1,
    survives == 1,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
  transmute(
    state, population, id, dormancy_spell,
    year_entry = year, logsize_entry = logsize_t0)

df_ra_entry_size <- df_ra_size %>%
  filter(year_t1 == year + 1L, is.finite(logsize_reactivate)) %>%
  transmute(
    state, population, id, dormancy_spell, year_ra = year,
    dormancy_year, logsize_reactivate) %>%
  inner_join(
    df_do_entry_size,
    by = c("state", "population", "id", "dormancy_spell"))

mod_ra_size <- lm(
  logsize_reactivate ~ logsize_entry,
  data = df_ra_entry_size)

summary(mod_ra_size)

df_ra_entry_size %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    correlation = cor(logsize_entry, logsize_reactivate))

fig_ra_size <- ggplot(
  df_ra_entry_size,
  aes(x = logsize_entry, y = logsize_reactivate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0, slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Dormancy entry vs reactivation size",
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = "log(leaf area) before dormancy",
    y = "log(leaf area) at reactivation") +
  theme_bw()

fig_ra_size


# Conditional reactivation size: mean depends on entry size.
# Use residual SD, not the marginal SD of all reactivation sizes.
react_b0 <- unname(coef(mod_ra_size)[["(Intercept)"]])
react_b1 <- unname(coef(mod_ra_size)[["logsize_entry"]])
react_sd <- sigma(mod_ra_size)
```

### Seed to recruit transition 
```{r}
# Seeds produced in year t are related to recruits observed in year t + 1.

# Total observed seed production per population and year.
df_re_seed <- df %>%
  group_by(
    population, year) %>%
  summarise(
    nr_seeds = sum(
      seed_nr,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    nr_seed_obs = sum(
      !is.na(seed_nr)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(
    nr_seed_obs > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    year_recruit = year + 1L)


# Number of recruits per sampled population and year.
df_re_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(
    population, year)

df_re_count <- df %>%
  filter(
    recruit == 1) %>%
  count(
    population, year,
    name = "nr_recruits")

df_re_count <- df_re_sampled %>%
  left_join(
    df_re_count,
    by = c(
      "population",
      "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    nr_recruits = replace_na(
      nr_recruits,
      0L))


# Match seed production at t to recruits at t + 1.
df_re <- df_re_seed %>%
  inner_join(
    df_re_count,
    by = c(
      "population",
      "year_recruit" = "year"))
```

```{r}
df_re_mod <- df_re %>%

mod_re <- lm(

summary(mod_re)

recr_per_seed <- unname(coef(mod_re)[["nr_seeds"]])

recr_per_seed
```

## Building the IPM from scratch
```{r}
extr_value <- function(x, field) {
  subset(x, coefficient == field)$value}

# Reference active abundance in the recruitment-fitting population-years.
df_re_n <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(persistence_t0), persistence_t0 != 'DEAD', dormant_t0 == 0) %>%
  group_by(population, year) %>%
  summarise(n_active = n_distinct(id), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  semi_join(df_re_mod, by = c('population', 'year'))

pars <- Filter(
  function(x) length(x) > 0,
  list(

    grow_b2 = extr_value(pars_gr, 'logsize_t0_2'),

    dorm_b0 = extr_value(pars_do, 'b0'),
```

## IPM functions
```{r}
grow_sd <- function(x, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * x))}


# Growth from size x to size y.
gxy <- function(x, y, pars, num_pars = v_mod_gr_index) {
  mean_value <- pars$grow_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('grow_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        mean_value <- mean_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  sd_value <- grow_sd(x, pars)
  dnorm(y, mean = mean_value, sd = sd_value)}


inv_logit <- function(x) {
  plogis(x)}


# Survival of an x-sized active individual.
sx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_su_index) {
  survival_value <- pars$surv_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('surv_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        survival_value <- survival_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(survival_value)}


# Dormancy entry conditional on survival.
dx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_do_index) {
  dorm_value <- pars$dorm_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('dorm_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        dorm_value <- dorm_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(dorm_value)}


# Flowering probability.
flx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_fl_index) {
  flower_value <- pars$flower_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('flower_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        flower_value <- flower_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(flower_value)}


# Positive seed production conditional on flowering.
sex <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_se_index) {
  seed_value <- pars$seed_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('seed_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        seed_value <- seed_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(seed_value)}


# Seed number conditional on positive seed production.
se_nx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_se_n_index) {
  seed_n_value <- pars$seed_n_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('seed_n_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        seed_n_value <- seed_n_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  exp(seed_n_value)}


# Expected seed production of an active individual.
seedx <- function(x, pars) {
  flx(x, pars) * sex(x, pars) * se_nx(x, pars)}


# Active survival-growth transition.
pxy <- function(x, y, pars) {
  sx(x, pars) * (1 - dx(x, pars)) * gxy(x, y, pars)}
```

## Kernel
```{r}
# Rows = destinations; columns = sources.
# 1:n = active; (n+1):(2*n) = dormant.
# Dormant plants retain size before dormancy.
# Non-return at the next census is treated as death.
kernel <- function(pars) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  i_dorm <- n + seq_len(n)
  
  # Growth distribution
  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  Gmat[] <- t(outer(y, y, gxy, pars)) * h
  
  # Eviction correction
  for (i in seq_len(n / 2)) {
    Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])}
  
  for (i in ((n / 2) + 1):n) {
    Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])}
  
  # Active survival and dormancy entry
  Smat <- sx(y, pars)
  Dvec <- dx(y, pars)
  Tmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i] * (1 - Dvec[i])}
  
  # Reactivation size conditional on entry size
  react_sd_use <- max(h / 10, pars$react_sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  Rmat <- vapply(y, function(x) {
    react_y <- dnorm(
      y, mean = pars$react_b0 + pars$react_b1 * x,
      sd = react_sd_use, log = TRUE)
    react_y <- exp(react_y - max(react_y))
    react_y / sum(react_y)}, numeric(n))
  
  # Recruit size distribution
  recr_sd_use <- max(h / 10, pars$recr_sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  recr_y <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = recr_sd_use) * h
  recr_y <- recr_y / sum(recr_y)
  
  Pmat <- matrix(0, 2 * n, 2 * n)
  Fmat <- matrix(0, 2 * n, 2 * n)
  
  # Active -> active
  Pmat[1:n, 1:n] <- Tmat
  
  # Active -> dormant: diagonal entry-size memory.
  Pmat[i_dorm, 1:n] <- diag(Smat * Dvec, nrow = n, ncol = n)
  
  # Dormant -> active: return probability and reactivation size.
  Pmat[1:n, i_dorm] <-
    pars$p_dorm_survival * pars$p_reactivate_1 * Rmat
  
  # Dormant -> dormant: no persistence; non-return is treated as death.
  Pmat[i_dorm, i_dorm] <- 0
  
  # Population intercept allocated per active plant at reference abundance.
  Fmat[1:n, 1:n] <- outer(
    recr_y,
    pars$recr_b0 / pars$recr_n_ref + pars$recr_per_seed * seedx(y, pars))
  
  k_yx <- Pmat + Fmat
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx, Pmat = Pmat, Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat, Gmat = Gmat, Rmat = Rmat,
    meshpts = y,
    dormant_index = i_dorm)}


lambda_ipm <- function(i) {
  Re(eigen(kernel(i)$k_yx)$values[1])}
```

## Building the IPM with ipmr
```{r}
proto_ipm_p <- init_ipm(
  sim_gen = 'general', di_dd = 'di', det_stoch = 'det') %>%
  
  # Active -> active
  define_kernel(
    name = 'P',
    family = 'CC',
    formula = s * (1 - p_do) * g * d_size,
    
    s = plogis(
      surv_b0 +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 1) surv_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 2) surv_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 3) surv_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    p_do = plogis(
      dorm_b0 +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 1) dorm_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 2) dorm_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 3) dorm_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    mu_g = grow_b0 +
      (if (mod_gr_index >= 1) grow_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
      (if (mod_gr_index >= 2) grow_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
      (if (mod_gr_index >= 3) grow_b3 * size_1^3 else 0),
    
    g = dnorm(size_2, mu_g, grow_sig),
    grow_sig = sqrt(a * exp(b * size_1)),
    
    data_list = pars,
    states = list(c('size')),
    uses_par_sets = FALSE,
    evict_cor = TRUE,
    evict_fun = truncated_distributions(fun = 'norm', target = 'g')) %>%
  
  # Active -> dormant
  define_kernel(
    name = 'D_enter',
    family = 'CC',
    formula = s * p_do * entry_memory * d_size,
    
    entry_memory = as.numeric(size_1 == dorm_2) / d_size,
    
    s = plogis(
      surv_b0 +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 1) surv_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 2) surv_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_su_index >= 3) surv_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    p_do = plogis(
      dorm_b0 +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 1) dorm_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 2) dorm_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_do_index >= 3) dorm_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    data_list = pars,
    states = list(c('size', 'dorm')),
    uses_par_sets = FALSE,
    evict_cor = FALSE) %>%
  
  # Dormant -> active
  define_kernel(
    name = 'D_leave',
    family = 'CC',
    formula = p_dorm_survival * p_reactivate_1 * r_d * d_dorm,
    
    react_mu = react_b0 + react_b1 * dorm_1,
    react_sig = max(d_size / 10, react_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    r_d = dnorm(size_2, react_mu, react_sig),
    
    data_list = pars,
    states = list(c('dorm', 'size')),
    uses_par_sets = FALSE,
    evict_cor = TRUE,
    evict_fun = truncated_distributions(fun = 'norm', target = 'r_d')) %>%
  
  # Dormant -> dormant: the all-zero block.
  define_kernel(
    name = 'D_stay',
    family = 'CC',
    formula = 0 * dorm_1 * dorm_2 * d_dorm,
    
    data_list = pars,
    states = list(c('dorm')),
    uses_par_sets = FALSE,
    evict_cor = FALSE) %>%
  
  # Active -> recruits: intercept and seed production both contribute.
  define_kernel(
    name = 'F',
    family = 'CC',
    formula =
      (recr_b0 / recr_n_ref + p_fl * p_se * n_se * recr_per_seed) *
      r_d * d_size,
    
    p_fl = plogis(
      flower_b0 +
        (if (mod_fl_index >= 1) flower_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_fl_index >= 2) flower_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_fl_index >= 3) flower_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    p_se = plogis(
      seed_b0 +
        (if (mod_se_index >= 1) seed_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_se_index >= 2) seed_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_se_index >= 3) seed_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    n_se = exp(
      seed_n_b0 +
        (if (mod_se_n_index >= 1) seed_n_b1 * size_1 else 0) +
        (if (mod_se_n_index >= 2) seed_n_b2 * size_1^2 else 0) +
        (if (mod_se_n_index >= 3) seed_n_b3 * size_1^3 else 0)),
    
    recr_sig = max(d_size / 10, recr_sd, na.rm = TRUE),
    r_d = dnorm(size_2, recr_sz, recr_sig),
    
    data_list = pars,
    states = list(c('size')),
    uses_par_sets = FALSE,
    evict_cor = TRUE,
    evict_fun = truncated_distributions(fun = 'norm', target = 'r_d')) %>%
  
  # Kernel implementation
  define_impl(
    make_impl_args_list(
      kernel_names = c('P', 'D_enter', 'D_leave', 'D_stay', 'F'),
      int_rule = rep('midpoint', 5),
      state_start = c('size', 'size', 'dorm', 'dorm', 'size'),
      state_end = c('size', 'dorm', 'size', 'dorm', 'size'))) %>%
  
  # Domains
  define_domains(
    size = c(pars$L, pars$U, pars$mat_siz),
    dorm = c(pars$L, pars$U, pars$mat_siz)) %>%
  
  # Initial population
  define_pop_state(
    pop_vectors = list(
      n_size = rep(1 / pars$mat_siz, pars$mat_siz),
      n_dorm = rep(0, pars$mat_siz)))


ipmr_p <- make_ipm(proto_ipm = proto_ipm_p, iterations = 200)


# Mean IPM population growth rate ---------------------------------------------
lam_mean_ipmr <- lambda(ipmr_p)
lam_mean_ipmr
```

# Mean mega matrix 3x3 {#mean_mega_3x3}

## Introduction
### Extension of the mega-matrix IPM to two years of dormancy

To accommodate individuals remaining dormant for more than one consecutive annual census, the original 2 × 2 mega-matrix was extended to a **3 × 3 block structure**. Whereas the previous model distinguished only between active and dormant individuals, the extended model separates dormancy into two successive states: first-year dormancy (\(D_1\)) and second-year dormancy (\(D_2\)). This modification allows individuals to remain dormant for up to two consecutive censuses before returning to the active population.

The extended projection matrix is defined as:

\[
\mathbf{K} =
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{T}+\mathbf{F} & \mathbf{R}_1 & \mathbf{R}_2\\
\mathbf{E} & \mathbf{0} & \mathbf{0}\\
\mathbf{0} & \mathbf{H} & \mathbf{0}
\end{pmatrix}
\]

The active survival-growth, fecundity, and dormancy-entry components remain unchanged from the original model. The principal modification concerns the transitions of individuals already in the dormant state.

In the original 2 × 2 matrix, individuals that did not reactivate after their first dormant census were removed from the projected population. The extended model instead introduces a transition from first-year to second-year dormancy, represented by the kernel \(\mathbf{H}\). Individuals surviving their first dormant year can either reactivate with probability \(r_1\) or remain dormant with probability \(1-r_1\). The transition into second-year dormancy is therefore defined as:

\[
H(y,x)=s_D(1-r_1)\delta(y-x)
\]

where \(s_D\) denotes annual dormant survival, \(r_1\) is the probability of reactivation conditional on survival, and \(\delta(y-x)\) preserves the individual's size before entering dormancy.

As in the original model, **dormant individuals retain their last observed active size**. This size-memory mechanism is extended to the second dormant state, allowing individuals to pass from \(D_1\) to \(D_2\) without losing information about their size at dormancy entry. Consequently, the transition between dormant states is represented by a diagonal matrix, rather than a growth distribution.

Reactivation is now possible from either dormant state. Individuals returning after their first dormant census follow the transition kernel:

\[
R_1(y,x)=s_Dr_1g_R(y\mid x)
\]

whereas individuals returning after their second dormant census follow:

\[
R_2(y,x)=s_Dg_R(y\mid x)
\]

Both reactivation kernels use the same conditional size distribution, \(g_R(y\mid x)\), which predicts reactivation size from the remembered size before dormancy. The distinction between the kernels lies in their reactivation probabilities. First-year dormant individuals may remain dormant, whereas **all surviving second-year dormant individuals are assumed to reactivate**.

The lower-right block consequently remains zero, preventing individuals from entering a third consecutive dormant year. The model therefore imposes a maximum of two dormant censuses, after which individuals either return to the active population or die.

This extension increases the dimensionality of the projection matrix from 400 × 400 to 600 × 600, with 200 size classes representing each of the three demographic states. All other demographic processes, including survival and growth of active individuals, dormancy entry, reproduction, and recruitment, retain their original formulation.

The extended mega-matrix thus relaxes the restrictive dormancy-duration assumption of the 2 × 2 model while preserving its size-memory framework. By explicitly distinguishing first- and second-year dormancy, it allows individuals to follow different temporal pathways back into the active population without introducing an unobservable growth process during dormancy.

```{r}
df <- read.csv(
```

## Survival rates
### Survival 
#### Data
```{r}
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 0,
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    state, population, id, year, size_t0, survives,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3)
```

#### Model
```{r}
mod_su_0 <- glm(
  survives ~ 1,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_1 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_2 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mod_su_3 <- glm(
  survives ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_su, family = 'binomial')

mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_1, mod_su_2, mod_su_3)

mods_su_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su}

mod_su_bestfit <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]

mod_su_bestfit
mods_su_dAICc
```

#### Plot
```{r}
df_su_newdata <- tibble(
  logsize_t0 = seq(
    min(df_su$logsize_t0),
    max(df_su$logsize_t0),
    length.out = 100)) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_t0_2 = logsize_t0^2,
    logsize_t0_3 = logsize_t0^3)

df_su_newdata$predicted <- predict(
  mod_su_bestfit,
  newdata = df_su_newdata,
  type = 'response')

fig_su_line <- ggplot(
  df_su,
  aes(x = logsize_t0, y = survives)) +
  geom_jitter(
    height = 0.05, width = 0,
    alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_su_newdata,
    aes(y = predicted),
    linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = 'Survival probability by size',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = expression('log(leaf area)'[t0]),
    y = 'Probability of survival') +
  theme_bw()


df_su_bindata <- plot_binned_prop(
  df_su, 10, logsize_t0, survives)

fig_su_bin <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(
    data = df_su_bindata,
    aes(x = logsize_t0, y = survives)) +
  geom_errorbar(
    data = df_su_bindata,
    aes(
      x = logsize_t0,
      ymin = lwr,
      ymax = upr),
    width = 0.1) +
  geom_line(
    data = df_su_newdata,
    aes(x = logsize_t0, y = predicted),
    linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    x = expression('log(leaf area)'[t0]),
    y = '') +
  theme_bw() +
  ylim(0, 1)

fig_su <- fig_su_line + fig_su_bin + plot_layout()
fig_su
```

### Dormant survival and reactivation
```{r}
# An active census, a gap, or an unconfirmed transition starts a new episode.
df_do_history <- df %>%
  group_by(state, population, id) %>%
  arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    dormancy_spell = cumsum(
      coalesce(dormant_t0 != 1, TRUE) |
        coalesce(year != lag(year_t1), TRUE) |
        !coalesce(lag(
          reliable_demography & survives == 1 & dormant_t1 == 1 &
            year_t1 == year + 1L), FALSE))) %>%
  ungroup()

# Identify entry even when the last active size was not measured.
# year_entry is the last active census; the first dormant census is +1.
df_do_entry <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography, dormant_t0 == 0, dormant_t1 == 1,
    survives == 1, year_t1 == year + 1L) %>%
  transmute(state, population, id, dormancy_spell, year_entry = year)

df_do_history <- df_do_history %>%
  left_join(
    df_do_entry, by = c("state", "population", "id", "dormancy_spell")) %>%
  mutate(dormancy_year = if_else(
    dormant_t0 == 1, as.integer(year - year_entry), NA_integer_))

df_ra <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    !is.na(survives))

# Share one annual dormant-survival estimate across both dormant stages.
mod_dorm_su <- glm(
  survives ~ 1,
  data = df_ra,
  family = "binomial")

p_dorm_survival <- predict(
  mod_dorm_su,
  newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
  type = "response")[1]


df_ra <- df_ra %>%
  filter(
    survives == 1,
    !is.na(dormant_t1)) %>%
  mutate(
    reactivate = as.integer(dormant_t1 == 0))

# Estimate first-year return from all surviving D1 transitions.
# Surviving D2 plants must return under the imposed two-census limit.
df_ra_1 <- df_ra %>%
  filter(dormancy_year == 1L)

mod_ra <- glm(
  reactivate ~ 1,
  data = df_ra_1,
  family = "binomial")

p_reactivate_1 <- predict(
  mod_ra,
  newdata = data.frame(x = 1),
  type = "response")[1]

# Diagnose observed spells extending beyond the imposed two-census limit.
# Include a confirmed D2 -> D3 even if no later source census is available.
df_dorm_over2 <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    dormancy_year > 2L |
      (dormancy_year == 2L & reliable_demography & survives == 1 &
         dormant_t1 == 1 & year_t1 == year + 1L)) %>%
  distinct(state, population, id, dormancy_spell)

df_ra %>%
  count(dormancy_year, reactivate, name = "n_transitions")

nrow(df_dorm_over2)


df_ra_size <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 1,
    survives == 1,
    dormant_t1 == 0,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    dormancy_year %in% c(1L, 2L),
    size_t1 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    logsize_reactivate = log(size_t1))
```

### Dormancy entry vs reactivation size
```{r}
# Fit return size to completed one- or two-census dormancy episodes.
# Longer observed spells are counted above, not relabelled as two years.

df_do_entry_size <- df_do_history %>%
  filter(
    reliable_demography,
    dormant_t0 == 0,
    dormant_t1 == 1,
    survives == 1,
    year_t1 == year + 1L,
    size_t0 > 0,
    is.finite(logsize_t0)) %>%
  transmute(
    state, population, id, dormancy_spell,
    year_entry = year, logsize_entry = logsize_t0)

df_ra_entry_size <- df_ra_size %>%
  filter(year_t1 == year + 1L, is.finite(logsize_reactivate)) %>%
  transmute(
    state, population, id, dormancy_spell, year_ra = year,
    dormancy_year, logsize_reactivate) %>%
  inner_join(
    df_do_entry_size,
    by = c("state", "population", "id", "dormancy_spell"))

mod_ra_size <- lm(
  logsize_reactivate ~ logsize_entry,
  data = df_ra_entry_size)

summary(mod_ra_size)

df_ra_entry_size %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    correlation = cor(logsize_entry, logsize_reactivate))

fig_ra_size <- ggplot(
  df_ra_entry_size,
  aes(x = logsize_entry, y = logsize_reactivate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_smooth(
    method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(
    intercept = 0, slope = 1,
    linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = "Dormancy entry vs reactivation size",
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = "log(leaf area) before dormancy",
    y = "log(leaf area) at reactivation") +
  theme_bw()

fig_ra_size


# Conditional reactivation size: mean depends on entry size.
# Use residual SD, not the marginal SD of all reactivation sizes.
react_b0 <- unname(coef(mod_ra_size)[["(Intercept)"]])
react_b1 <- unname(coef(mod_ra_size)[["logsize_entry"]])
react_sd <- sigma(mod_ra_size)
```

```{r}
  data = df_se,
  family = "binomial")

mod_se_2 <- glm(
  seed_prod ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2,
  data = df_se,
  family = "binomial")

mod_se_3 <- glm(
  seed_prod ~ logsize_t0 + logsize_t0_2 + logsize_t0_3,
  data = df_se,
  family = "binomial")

mods_se <- list(
  mod_se_0, mod_se_1, mod_se_2, mod_se_3)

mods_se_dAICc <- AICctab(
  mods_se,
  weights = TRUE,
  sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_se_sorted <- order(mods_se_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_se) == 0) {
  mod_se_index_bestfit <- mods_se_sorted[1]
  v_mod_se_index <- mod_se_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_se_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_se + 1
  v_mod_se_index <- v_mod_set_se
}

mod_se_bestfit <- mods_se[[mod_se_index_bestfit]]

mod_se_bestfit
mods_se_dAICc
```

#### Data

```{r}
  group_by(
    population, year) %>%
  summarise(
    nr_seeds = sum(
      seed_nr,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    nr_seed_obs = sum(
      !is.na(seed_nr)),
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(
    nr_seed_obs > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    year_recruit = year + 1L)


# Number of recruits per sampled population and year.
df_re_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(
    population, year)

  filter(
    recruit == 1) %>%
  count(
    population, year,
    name = "nr_recruits")

  left_join(
    df_re_count,
    by = c(
      "population",
      "year")) %>%
  mutate(
    nr_recruits = replace_na(
      nr_recruits,
      0L))


# Match seed production at t to recruits at t + 1.
df_re <- df_re_seed %>%
  inner_join(
    df_re_count,
    by = c(
      "population",
      "year_recruit" = "year"))
```

```{r}
extr_value <- function(x, field) {
  subset(x, coefficient == field)$value}

  semi_join(df_re_mod, by = c('population', 'year'))
```

## IPM functions
```{r}
grow_sd <- function(x, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * x))}


# Growth from size x to size y.
gxy <- function(x, y, pars, num_pars = v_mod_gr_index) {
  mean_value <- pars$grow_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('grow_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        mean_value <- mean_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  sd_value <- grow_sd(x, pars)
  dnorm(y, mean = mean_value, sd = sd_value)}


inv_logit <- function(x) {
  plogis(x)}


# Survival of an x-sized active individual.
sx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_su_index) {
  survival_value <- pars$surv_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('surv_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        survival_value <- survival_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(survival_value)}


# Dormancy entry conditional on survival.
dx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_do_index) {
  dorm_value <- pars$dorm_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('dorm_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        dorm_value <- dorm_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(dorm_value)}


# Flowering probability.
flx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_fl_index) {
  flower_value <- pars$flower_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('flower_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        flower_value <- flower_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(flower_value)}


# Positive seed production conditional on flowering.
sex <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_se_index) {
  seed_value <- pars$seed_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('seed_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        seed_value <- seed_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  inv_logit(seed_value)}


# Seed number conditional on positive seed production.
se_nx <- function(x, pars, num_pars = v_mod_se_n_index) {
  seed_n_value <- pars$seed_n_b0
  
  if (num_pars >= 1) {
    for (i in seq_len(num_pars)) {
      param_name <- paste0('seed_n_b', i)
      if (!is.null(pars[[param_name]])) {
        seed_n_value <- seed_n_value + pars[[param_name]] * x^i}}}
  
  exp(seed_n_value)}


# Expected seed production of an active individual.
seedx <- function(x, pars) {
  flx(x, pars) * sex(x, pars) * se_nx(x, pars)}


# Active survival-growth transition.
pxy <- function(x, y, pars) {
  sx(x, pars) * (1 - dx(x, pars)) * gxy(x, y, pars)}
```

## Kernel
```{r}
# Rows = destinations; columns = sources.
# 1:n = active; (n+1):(2*n) = D1; (2*n+1):(3*n) = D2.
# Both dormant stages retain the size at dormancy entry.
# No D2 -> D2 transition: surviving D2 plants must reactivate.
kernel <- function(pars) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  i_dorm1 <- n + seq_len(n)
  i_dorm2 <- 2 * n + seq_len(n)
  
  # Growth distribution
  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  Gmat[] <- t(outer(y, y, gxy, pars)) * h
  
  # Eviction correction
  for (i in seq_len(n / 2)) {
    Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])}
  
  for (i in ((n / 2) + 1):n) {
    Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])}
  
  # Active survival and dormancy entry
  Smat <- sx(y, pars)
  Dvec <- dx(y, pars)
  Tmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i] * (1 - Dvec[i])}
  
  # Reactivation size conditional on entry size
  react_sd_use <- max(h / 10, pars$react_sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  Rmat <- vapply(y, function(x) {
    react_y <- dnorm(
      y, mean = pars$react_b0 + pars$react_b1 * x,
      sd = react_sd_use, log = TRUE)
    react_y <- exp(react_y - max(react_y))
    react_y / sum(react_y)}, numeric(n))
  
  # Recruit size distribution
  recr_sd_use <- max(h / 10, pars$recr_sd, na.rm = TRUE)
  recr_y <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = recr_sd_use) * h
  recr_y <- recr_y / sum(recr_y)
  
  Pmat <- matrix(0, 3 * n, 3 * n)
  Fmat <- matrix(0, 3 * n, 3 * n)
  
  # Active -> active
  Pmat[1:n, 1:n] <- Tmat
  
  # Active -> D1: diagonal entry-size memory.
  Pmat[i_dorm1, 1:n] <- diag(Smat * Dvec, nrow = n, ncol = n)

  # D1 -> active: first-year return probability and reactivation size.
  Pmat[1:n, i_dorm1] <-
    pars$p_dorm_survival * pars$p_reactivate_1 * Rmat

  # D1 -> D2: surviving non-reactivators retain their entry size.
  Pmat[i_dorm2, i_dorm1] <- diag(
    pars$p_dorm_survival * (1 - pars$p_reactivate_1),
    nrow = n, ncol = n)

  # D2 -> active: all surviving second-year dormant plants reactivate.
  Pmat[1:n, i_dorm2] <- pars$p_dorm_survival * Rmat

  # All other dormant transitions are zero (no third dormant year).

  # Population intercept allocated per active plant at reference abundance.
  Fmat[1:n, 1:n] <- outer(
    recr_y,
    pars$recr_b0 / pars$recr_n_ref + pars$recr_per_seed * seedx(y, pars))
  
  k_yx <- Pmat + Fmat
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx, Pmat = Pmat, Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat, Gmat = Gmat, Rmat = Rmat,
    meshpts = y,
    dormant_index = c(i_dorm1, i_dorm2),
    dormant1_index = i_dorm1,
    dormant2_index = i_dorm2)}


lambda_ipm <- function(i) {
  Re(eigen(kernel(i)$k_yx)$values[1])}
```
